\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عیادت} \ur{کرنا} (iyādat karnā)}{عیادت کرنا (iyādat karnā)}]{\ur{عیادت} \ur{کرنا} (iyādat karnā) — to visit the sick}

\label{lesson:UR-C480-iyadat-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a surgeon, then the Urdu for a stretcher.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عیادت} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{عیادت} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{iyādat karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to visit the sick\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہم} \ur{نے} \ur{ہسپتال} \ur{جا} \ur{کر} \ur{دادا} \ur{کی} \ur{عیادت} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ham ne haspatāl jā kar dādā kī iyādat kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We went to the hospital to visit my grandfather.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مریض} \ur{کی} \ur{عیادت} \ur{کی}, \emph{us ne marīz kī iyādat kī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عیادت} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{iyādat karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{عیادت}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿiyāda}, \textquotedblleft{}visiting the sick\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iyādat karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iyādat karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ham ne haspatāl jā kar dādā kī iyādat kī.} — We went to the hospital to visit my grandfather.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a surgeon, then the Urdu for a stretcher, then say \emph{iyādat karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{عیادت} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To visit the sick\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تیمارداری} (tīmārdārī)}{تیمارداری (tīmārdārī)}]{\ur{تیمارداری} (tīmārdārī) — nursing the sick}

\label{lesson:UR-C480-timardari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a stretcher, then the Urdu for to visit the sick.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تیمارداری}}
\textbf{\ur{تیمارداری}} — \emph{tīmārdārī} — \textquotedblleft{}nursing the sick\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بہن} \ur{نے} \ur{رات} \ur{بھر} \ur{ماں} \ur{کی} \ur{تیمارداری} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bahan ne rāt bhar māṅ kī tīmārdārī kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister nursed our mother all night.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تیمارداری}} (\emph{tīmārdārī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{tīmārdārī}, \textquotedblleft{}tending the sick\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{tīmār}, \textquotedblleft{}care\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīmārdārī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīmārdārī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahan ne rāt bhar māṅ kī tīmārdārī kī.} — My sister nursed our mother all night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a stretcher, then the Urdu for to visit the sick, then say \emph{tīmārdārī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نگہداشت} (nigahdāsht)}{نگہداشت (nigahdāsht)}]{\ur{نگہداشت} (nigahdāsht) — care; looking after}

\label{lesson:UR-C480-nigahdasht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to visit the sick, then the Urdu for nursing the sick.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نگہداشت}}
\textbf{\ur{نگہداشت}} — \emph{nigahdāsht} — \textquotedblleft{}care; looking after\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بوڑھوں} \ur{کو} \ur{اچھی} \ur{نگہداشت} \ur{کی} \ur{ضرورت} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{būṛhoṅ ko achchhī nigahdāsht kī zarūrat hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نگہداشت}} (\emph{nigahdāsht}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{nigahdāsht}, \textquotedblleft{}keeping, guarding\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لٹانا} (liṭānā)}{لٹانا (liṭānā)}]{\ur{لٹانا} (liṭānā) — to lay (someone) down}

\label{lesson:UR-C480-litana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for nursing the sick, then the Urdu for looking after.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لٹانا}}
\textbf{\ur{لٹانا}} — \emph{liṭānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to lay (someone) down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نرس} \ur{نے} \ur{مریض} \ur{کو} \ur{بستر} \ur{پر} \ur{لٹایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nars ne marīz ko bistar par liṭāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The nurse laid the patient on the bed.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{لٹایا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko liṭāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لٹانا}} (\emph{liṭānā}) is the causative of \textbf{\ur{لیٹنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to lie down\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{lēṭyáti} (CDIAL 11109).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{liṭānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{liṭānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nars ne marīz ko bistar par liṭāyā.} — The nurse laid the patient on the bed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for nursing the sick, then the Urdu for looking after, then say \emph{liṭānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{لٹانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To lay (someone) down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اوڑھانا} (oṛhānā)}{اوڑھانا (oṛhānā)}]{\ur{اوڑھانا} (oṛhānā) — to cover someone up (with a blanket)}

\label{lesson:UR-C480-orhana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for looking after, then the Urdu for to lay (someone) down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اوڑھانا}}
\textbf{\ur{اوڑھانا}} — \emph{oṛhānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to cover someone up (with a blanket)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{کمبل} \ur{اوڑھایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ ne bachche ko kambal oṛhāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother tucked a blanket over the child.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مریض} \ur{کو} \ur{کمبل} \ur{اوڑھایا}, \emph{us ne marīz ko kambal oṛhāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اوڑھانا}} (\emph{oṛhānā}) is the causative of \emph{oṛhnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to wrap oneself in\textquotedblright{}, inherited from \emph{ōḍḍh}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 2547).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṛhānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māṅ ne bachche ko kambal oṛhāyā.} — The mother tucked a blanket over the child.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for looking after, then the Urdu for to lay (someone) down, then say \emph{oṛhānā} again
\end{itemize}
